about: Web research done before the final rebuild (2026-10-05). Used only to improve filmmaking craft; it never overrides verified Navis product capabilities. Nothing from these sources (words, branding, animation) is copied into the film.
honest_limits: Web search was available, but it returned mostly generic launch-video advice and company profiles. No retrievable source analysed the actual cuts, timing or typography of the Kanu, Cursor, Claude Code, Lovable, Manus, ElevenLabs, Firecrawl or Perplexity launch films.
So the notes below are principles plus what could be confirmed about the companies, not a shot-by-shot study of their films.

sources.used_for: Product storytelling as a narrative a buyer can follow and remember, rather than a feature list.
Simplify the technical idea, humanize it, build trust, create a memorable moment, establish the company's voice. No named examples in the article.
Earn attention in the first seconds; name the specific job, not the category.
The cursor as a visible protagonist that walks the eye to the next point of interest and causes the next thing to happen.
YC-style structure: hook, problem, demo, vision; founder narration; clarity over production value.
Kanu AI positioning only (an AI cloud engineer that ships inside AWS environments). Its launch film itself was not found.
Confirms Claude Code launched as a standalone developer product in 2025 and runs in the terminal and in VS Code. Supports showing Claude Code inside VS Code's integrated terminal.

principles_applied.principle: Open on the idea, then prove it with something concrete within seconds.
principles_applied.in_the_film: Line 1 states the thesis; lines 2–6 each land on a concrete signal card from one real-looking company story (decision, customer, commitment, meeting, context).

principles_applied.principle: Name the job, not the category.
principles_applied.in_the_film: 'What does this company already know?' is the question every task starts with; the products answer it for people and for agents.

principles_applied.principle: Real input, real output: show the product working before explaining it.
principles_applied.in_the_film: Navis Application: Today → why → trace → draft → human edit → approve → Gmail confirms. Navis Developer: task → context request → facts with source and freshness → work state → permission → the agent continues.
Every click moves the story: 'Why this matters', 'Review & reply', 'Review draft', the sentence selection, 'Approve & send'. No decorative cursor travel.

principles_applied.principle: Founder voice, calm, with pauses where the picture must do the work.
principles_applied.in_the_film: The voice track leaves silent windows during the trace, the edit and send, the context results and the refusal.

principles_applied.principle: Product is the hero; motion clarifies.
principles_applied.in_the_film: Macro crops and hard cuts within real UI instead of decorative motion graphics; one cobalt line (the logo colour) is the only accent.
The final card is the NavisLabs lockup, the two products, ONE SHARED UNDERSTANDING and navislabs.in.

deliberately_not_adopted: Metrics in the first 10 seconds (common YC advice): NavisLabs has no approved public metrics, so none are shown.
Traction, logo walls and investor asks: not approved; not in the film.
